newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish opposition proposes flood relief bonds.
newsitem.headline: Polish opposition proposes flood relief bonds.

text.p: Poland's biggest opposition grouping, Solidarity Election Alliance (AWS), proposed on Thursday that the government issue special bonds to raise funds for flooded areas, PAP news agency said.
Under the plan, unveiled in AWS's "Programme to Finance the Reconstruction of Flooded Areas," part of the cost of the bonds could be deducted from personal income tax.
The paper, maturing after one, three and five years, would have a fixed coupon.
"We want the programme, prepared by our experts, to be taken into account by parliament and the government," PAP quoted AWS's deputy head Janusz Tomaszewski as saying.
AWS is the strongest challenger to the ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance party in elections due on September 21.

The grouping wants the bonds to generate means for creating a fund that would invest in southern and western regions, where this month's prolonged floods inundated 6,000 sq km, killing 55 people, damaging many roads, bridges and buildings.

The fund would also repay loans taken by the government from the central bank for flood relief purposes. As an emergency measure, parliament has authorised the government to draw up to 2.5 billion zlotys ($728 million) on the National Bank of Poland this year.
Officials of the government, which has not planned any issues of treasuries specifically to finance its flood relief scheme, were not immediately available for comment on the AWS proposals.
